key_insight: Compact multimodal models can support pulmonary embolism question answering best when CT angiography is combined with EHR evidence, especially for diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: The study suggests efficient MLLMs may help early PE risk assessment and clinical explanation, but prognostic prediction remains harder than diagnosis.
method: Built the INSPECT benchmark with 23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients.
Framed 8 PE diagnostic and prognostic tasks as structured clinical QA.
Compared efficient MLLMs across CTPA-only, EHR-only, and CTPA+EHR settings using zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
evidence_signal: Across benchmark evaluations, Gemma4 E4B and Gemma4 E2B performed best when EHR evidence was added, with diagnosis outperforming prognostic tasks overall.
watch_item: Performance in this benchmark does not guarantee safe real-world use, especially for readmission prediction and other prognostic tasks.
paper_title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment
